reviewMethod: Manual route-by-route review of headings, labels, table headers, filters, actions, badges, helper text, states, confirmations, disclosures, and generated labels.

findings.outcome: Reduced to three strong sections while preserving the hero.
Now states that portfolio and priorities are confirmed before workspace creation.
Completion states describe sign-in progress and recovery only.

findings.issue: Role and workspace-access distinction is verbose
findings.outcome: Kept concise because it prevents an access-control mistake.
Role priority queue shows actionable non-zero work before portfolio context.
Detail view leads with the selected queue or analysis.
Restore consequence now names active property lists.
Readiness now names required checks and records.
Identity remains in the record header and unresolved readiness stays near its repair action.
Surface is labeled Current balances and retains the official-statement warning.

findings.issue: Portfolio-wide finance context obscures the current Property
findings.outcome: The Property record now leads with scoped rent, expenses, and owner account links.
Canonical links replace repeated detail blocks.

findings.issue: Unit finance requires repeated global filtering
findings.outcome: The Unit record opens rent and expenses already scoped to the Unit.
Copy now names People lists, linked work, and record roles directly.
Only the workspace-access distinction remains.
Owner record actions name property ownership and reporting.

findings.issue: Role and workspace access can be confused
findings.outcome: Kept a concise distinction between staff record and workspace access.
Tenant copy names leases, occupancy, and follow-up.
Vendor copy names service work and maintenance links.
Lease consequence uses Rent terms.

findings.issue: Lifecycle actions and lease context compete on one surface
findings.outcome: The record is split into focused sections and keeps the next lifecycle action with its evidence.
Manager and member homes use Review queue and My finance work.

findings.issue: Ledger, petty cash, and historical policies compete with daily finance work
findings.outcome: Specialized and historical tools now sit behind one Advanced finance entry.

findings.issue: Source mechanics compete with rent decisions
findings.outcome: Primary view leads with tenant, amount, due status, and legitimate action.

findings.issue: Evidence hash appears in task rows
findings.outcome: File name and size remain visible; fingerprint is under Audit details.

findings.issue: Authority, roll-forward, remediation, hashes, watermarks, IDs, and JSON dominate the task view
findings.outcome: Operator view uses owner balances, calculate month, source issues, and balance sources; exact provenance is labeled and closed by default.

findings.issue: Raw native controls and status colors
findings.outcome: Shared SelectControl and semantic Badge/token treatments are used.

findings.issue: Empty state refers to source workflows and operational events
findings.outcome: Empty state says no financial transactions are recorded.

findings.issue: Reconciliation terminology is necessary for cash movements
findings.outcome: Kept where it distinguishes non-ledger cash advances and posting consequences.
Tabs, filters, and PDF/Excel actions carry the meaning.

findings.issue: Generic workflow label and restore explanation
findings.outcome: Current stage and active maintenance lists name the operator task directly.
Operations Member home is My work and exposes assigned actions only.
Event, actor, scope, exact time, and Open record carry the meaning.
URL scope and record links are canonical.
Maintenance event, actor, time, and source record remain.
Financial event and authoritative source link remain.

findings.issue: Hash/storage implementation could displace evidence task
findings.outcome: Default view uses document, category, linked record, and availability; integrity values are not primary copy.

findings.issue: Cutover authority, reconciliation SHA-256, request keys, and manifest JSON are primary
findings.outcome: Import cutover, start date, imported records, mismatches, and approval reason lead; manifest and fingerprints are disclosed and request keys hidden.

findings.issue: Organization and personal theme ownership can be confused
findings.outcome: Copy keeps the organization default versus personal display distinction.

findings.issue: Workspace name and address ownership can be confused
findings.outcome: The name is editable while the provisioned workspace address is clearly locked and copyable.

findings.issue: Organization theme and personal display preference can be confused
findings.outcome: The section states which choices affect every workspace member.

findings.issue: Member, person, staff, role, and scope can be conflated
findings.outcome: Concise access-boundary copy remains beside invite and role changes.

findings.issue: Permission changes can affect active access
findings.outcome: The editor states the affected user count before permissions are removed or a role is archived.

findings.issue: Member, person, staff, role, and scope can be conflated
findings.outcome: Concise access-boundary copy remains beside invite and role changes.
